summary: Backend testing completed for two new requirements: (1) Process cost per unit on inhouse operations with BOM explosion costing, (2) SC order consolidation for same supplier. All 9 tests passed.
seed_data_creation: Test data created dynamically with TEST_ prefix for items, BOMs, routings, suppliers, production orders, and work orders
context_for_next_testing_agent: All tests for process_cost_per_unit and SC consolidation pass. Key findings: (1) BOM must have status='active' for operations to be created on MO, (2) Operations must be stopped/completed before starting next operation, (3) SC consolidation works when outsourcing multiple operations to same supplier - charges and operation sequences are merged, (4) Different suppliers create separate SC orders as expected.
tests_passed: test_04_process_cost_persists_on_complete - process_cost_per_unit persists on completed operations
test_06_outsource_first_operation_creates_sc - First outsourced operation creates new SC order
test_07_second_outsource_same_supplier_consolidates - Second outsourced operation to same supplier consolidates into existing SC (charges merged, operation sequences merged)
test_08_dc_updated_with_merged_lines - Draft DC is updated with merged lines
test_09_different_supplier_creates_separate_sc - Outsourcing to different supplier creates separate SC order

req1_process_cost_per_unit.details: process_cost_per_unit field saves on operation start and persists on completion. BOM explosion returns process_cost_per_unit and total_cost_per_unit fields.

req2_sc_consolidation.details: When outsourcing multiple operations to same supplier, they consolidate into single SC order. Processing charges are summed (100+150=250), operation sequences are merged ([10,20]), and DC lines are updated. Different suppliers create separate SC orders.
